verdict.rationale: Link CLI gives an agent access to a customer-controlled Link wallet. The agent can pull one-time-use virtual cards or SPTs and read balances from accounts the user connects, which covers user control and balance visibility. However, it is not a funded wallet the agent holds and spends from on its own: every spend needs the customer's approval, and balances come from linked bank and card accounts rather than a provisioned wallet balance. Missing for 10: a prefunded agent-held wallet balance, a documented top-up/funding flow, standing spend authority without per-request approval, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can provision a wallet my agent holds and spends from — funded and controlled by me, with balance visibility

citations.quote: Link CLI gives your agent access to a wallet that your customer controls. Your agent can retrieve one-time-use payment credentials to complete purchases
Your agent reads transaction history, balances, and account details from connected bank accounts and credit cards.
Customers approve each request on the Link website or in the mobile app.
Creates a spend request for a specific purchase. The customer approves it, and Link returns a one-time-use payment credential your agent uses to pay.
